title: Oscar and the Playlist
premise: Odile Eastwick has spent four years keeping her head down at Marsh Hollow High, raising her siblings while her mother works night shifts, counting the days to graduation like a get-out-of-jail sentence. When she finds her late grandmother's recipe box hiding coded directions instead of recipes, she uncovers a paper trail proving the school board buried a toxic water contamination scandal that explains her grandmother's illness—and her own brother's. As she and Oscar Reyes, the school's charming outcast with a playlist for every mood, dig deeper, Odile must choose between staying invisible long enough to escape, or burning her one shot at a clean exit by exposing the truth before prom. She chooses truth: the board resigns in disgrace, the town gets clean water funding, and Odile walks into graduation not as someone escaping her life, but as someone who finally owns it.
about_author: Vesper Nystrom is a former small-town newspaper reporter who writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse to wait their turn. She lives near a lake she refuses to swim in, on principle.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A morning montage of toast, permission slips, and dragging her brother Theo to school establishes her caretaker role and her countdown calendar—87 days to graduation. Emotional beat: weary resignation disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Recipe Box Rules
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Cleaning out Grandma June's attic, she finds the recipe box; among index cards are instructions referencing 'the well log' and 'Room 12.' Beat: first crack of curiosity through grief.

chapters.title: Oscar's Soundtrack
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Detention-adjacent intro: Oscar shares earbuds with Odile during a fire drill, narrating his playlist philosophy—one song per feeling. Beat: reluctant delight; she hasn't felt seen in years.

chapters.title: Card #7: Simmer Uncovered
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Decoding card seven reveals coordinates matching the old mill site and a date from 1998. Beat: unease—the recipe box isn't nostalgia, it's evidence.

chapters.title: Theo's Cough
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Theo's persistent cough sends them to the clinic; the doctor mentions 'a cluster of cases' then goes quiet when asked. Beat: protective fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Room 12
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile and Oscar sneak into the school annex after hours; Room 12 is now storage, but the floor tiles hide an old filing cabinet footprint. Beat: conspiratorial thrill, first real alliance.

chapters.title: The Board President's Smile
chapters.summary: Odile POV. At a school board meeting, Odile watches Chairman Dale Pruitt deflect a parent's question about water testing with practiced charm. Beat: cold recognition of how power performs innocence.

chapters.title: Playlist for Stakeouts
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Oscar builds her a playlist titled 'For Girls Who Can't Sleep'; they stake out county records office, finding a redacted 1999 well report. Beat: intimacy blooming inside danger.

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Her mother, exhausted and defensive, warns her to stop asking about Grandma June—'some things cost more than they pay.' Beat: guilt; duty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: The Librarian Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Retired librarian Mrs. Okonkwo confirms June Eastwick was a water board clerk who was fired after requesting independent tests. Beat: validation; grandma becomes a person, not just a loss.

chapters.title: Card #19: Serve Cold
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Card nineteen lists names of five families—including hers—who received quiet settlements. Beat: betrayal; the hush money bought her childhood silence.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Comic relief chapter: Oscar gets drafted onto prom committee as cover, discovering the venue is Pruitt's country club. Beat: levity laced with irony.

chapters.title: Someone Went Through My Locker
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Her decoded notes vanish from her locker; a warning note appears: 'Graduate quietly.' Beat: dread; the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: The Settlement Check
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Digging through family papers, she finds the actual settlement check—signed by her mother. Beat: heartbreak; mom knew, and chose survival over justice.

chapters.title: Confrontation at 2 A.M.
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile confronts her mother between shifts; Mom confesses she took the money because Theo needed surgery. Beat: devastating empathy—duty vs. truth cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Oscar's Secret
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Reversal: Oscar admits his father was the mill's site manager who signed off on the dumping. Beat: shame and vulnerability; he joined the investigation to atone.

chapters.title: Burned Bridge, Borrowed Car
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With Odile grounded and Oscar disowned for a night, they drive to the mill ruins anyway. Beat: defiant freedom; love declared without saying it.

chapters.title: What the Water Did
chapters.summary: Odile POV. At the mill they find corroded drums and take samples; Oscar explains what his father confessed before dying. Beat: grim clarity—the contamination is ongoing, not historical.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Daughter
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okonkwo POV (interlude). The librarian reveals June died believing no one would ever listen. Beat: inheritance of unfinished courage.

chapters.title: Leak Test
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They send samples to a state lab anonymously and draft an exposé for the student paper. Beat: nervous momentum; point of no return approaching.

chapters.title: Pruitt Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Pruitt corners Odile: full scholarship, tuition paid, if she hands over everything. Beat: temptation crystallized—her escape, priced exactly right.

chapters.title: The Countdown Breaks
chapters.summary: Odile POV. She tears down her graduation countdown calendar. Beat: quiet turning point—she stops serving time and starts spending it.

chapters.title: Allies Emerge
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Classmates, the paper's editor, and two teachers quietly join; even Theo insists on helping. Beat: solidarity replacing isolation.

chapters.title: Card #31: Garnish Before Serving
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Final decoded card instructs where June hid the original unredacted reports—in the church organ loft. Beat: awe at grandma's foresight.

chapters.title: Organ Loft
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A tense retrieval scene mid-Sunday service; they find the documents but are photographed leaving. Beat: triumph shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Odile POV. The school suspends both of them for 'break and entering' days before prom. Beat: public humiliation; the machine fights back.

chapters.title: Mom Chooses Sides
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Her mother, seeing the lab results confirming Theo's illness, brings her own copy of the settlement file. Beat: reconciliation; the family becomes a team.

chapters.title: Prom Eve Press Run
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. The student paper prints overnight in a borrowed garage; Oscar curates a playlist for the printing press. Beat: giddy, exhausted hope.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They attend prom under suspension threat; Pruitt publicly congratulates them, a trap. Beat: glittering tension; the calm before detonation.

chapters.title: Front Page Friday
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The exposé drops: contamination, settlements, cover-up, named officials. The town erupts. Beat: shockwave; nothing will be invisible again.

chapters.title: State Investigators
chapters.summary: Odile POV. State investigators arrive; Pruitt spins, but the unredacted reports hold. Beat: vindication tempered by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Backlash
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Half the town vilifies them—jobs threatened, windows egged. Beat: the cost of truth made tangible.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Odile POV. School board hearing on their suspension becomes a referendum; testimony from affected families floods in. Beat: communal catharsis.

chapters.title: Pruitt Falls
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Pruitt resigns as federal water funding is announced; his final glare promises this isn't over. Beat: victory with a bruise.

chapters.title: Reinstated
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Suspension lifted; classmates applaud in the hallway—a moment she once would have dreaded. Beat: visibility survived.

chapters.title: Grandma's Grave
chapters.summary: Odile POV. She reads the front page aloud at June's grave and leaves the recipe box's last blank card, finally filled in. Beat: grief transmuted into gratitude.

chapters.title: A Song for Graduation
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Oscar finishes the playlist's final track: 'For Odile, who stayed.' He plays it for her on the empty auditorium stage. Beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Graduation day; Odile crosses the stage as her siblings scream her name, no longer counting days. Beat: earned joy; the sentence commuted.

chapters.title: The Last Recipe
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Epilogue: summer begins, Theo healthy, mom on day shifts, Odile interning at the county paper. She starts a new recipe box—with real recipes, and one blank card left open. Beat: forward-looking peace.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Oscar POV. Coda: Oscar presses play on a shared playlist called 'Everything After,' and Odile takes his hand. Beat: open-hearted ending—love and truth, both chosen.
